candidate.title: UMI Method
candidate.scope: The assigned poster row labelled UMI Method: a poly(A)-bearing mRNA-fragment route through first-strand synthesis, the depicted P5/index/N10-associated second-strand synthesis, PCR, and tag-family sequence interpretation. The catalogue heading UMI: Unique Molecular Identifiers describes the same target and repeats these captions. This is a schematic architecture, not an assertion that all UMI implementations use this preparation. Neighboring scRNA-seq, SUPeR-seq, Digital RNA/HiRes-Seq/FREQ-Seq rows and the separate chemical panel have no connecting route into this target and are excluded.

features: Two paired lines show the RNA template and its copied strand, with A-rich/T-rich pairing.

states.label: cDNA intermediate after depicted second-strand synthesis
features: A second copied strand is shown with a P5-labelled extension, an Index, and a Degenerate molecular tag (N10).

operations.label: Second strand synthesis
operations.description: Illumina depicts an additional copied strand and the P5/Index/N10-containing linker at the step captioned Second strand synthesis, yielding its tagged pre-PCR intermediate. operations.mechanism: Primary-paper interpretation: reverse-transcriptase template switching introduces the N10-bearing 5′ adaptor during cDNA synthesis, followed by direct PCR of the resulting cDNA. Illumina’s caption does not independently establish a separate conventional second-strand reaction as the label-incorporation mechanism.
operations.information_effect: A degenerate 10-base label is physically linked to the transcript-derived cDNA before PCR; the separately labelled index has a different role. In the cited implementation, the label and mapped 5′ fragment position together define the UMI, with reads also assigned to a gene.
